target: NVIDIA GR00T / Unitree G1 (29 body DoF + two Dex3 hands) in Isaac Sim
reads: timeline/frames.jsonl (bone_rotations_xyzw, hips_position, pose_canonical, finger_curls_rad, phase, caption)
human/pose_landmarks.csv (paired normalized-image and canonical landmarks, for the image-plane fit)

robot.kinematics_source: g1_29dof_with_hand.urdf, the official Unitree G1 description (unitree_ros), as redistributed in NVIDIA GR00T-WholeBodyControl at gr00t_wbc/control/robot_model/model_data/g1/
robot.note: hardware. Not one number here is derived from the dataset, and none of it was stretched to fit the subject

coordinate_conversion.robot: URDF/ROS: Z-up, X forward, Y left, origin at the pelvis
coordinate_conversion.canonical_to_robot: (x, y, z) -> (z, x, y); a permutation with determinant +1, so a rotation and not a flip
coordinate_conversion.robot_to_stage: -90 deg about Z, carried by the /World/G1 root Xform

retarget.method: per-frame damped least squares on segment *direction* residuals, warm-started from the previous frame, with the URDF's joint limits as box constraints
retarget.matched: upper arm, forearm, hand axis and palm normal (arms); thigh, shank and foot forward (legs); the torso's rotation relative to the pelvis, decomposed in the waist chain's own Z-X-Y order (waist)
retarget.not_matched: absolute positions in metres. The G1's segments are shorter than the subject's, so matching a reach in metres would need either a resized robot or a fabricated pose

scale.definition: robot seated pelvis height (from its retargeted leg pose, with factory link lengths) divided by the subject's pelvis height above the derived floor
scale.applied_to: floor, chair, table and camera -- not to the robot

scale: the whole set is scaled by 0.8352 about the floor plane -- the ratio of the robot's own seated pelvis height (from its retargeted leg pose, with its factory link lengths) to the subject's. The robot is not resized; the room is
chair: seat height: derived from the canonical pelvis position (the subject is sitting on it)
width and back height: projected_to_plane from the median of 144 `chair` detections
table: top height: the height the right hand reached at frame 29 (t=2.42s), its furthest reach
radius and X: projected_to_plane from the median of 26 `dining table` detections

groot_dataset.embodiment: Isaac Lab Arena G1 (43-DoF joint space, `modality.json` groups: left_leg, right_leg, waist, left_arm, left_hand, right_arm, right_hand)
groot_dataset.state_and_action: the 43 joint angles in radians, in that order
groot_dataset.action_definition: action[t] = state[t+1], last frame repeated -- a kinematic replay, not a policy rollout
groot_dataset.eef_pose: [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz] of each hand's palm link, **in the pelvis frame** (X forward, Y left, Z up), left then right

filled_or_interpolated: finger curls: 9/96 left frames had no hand detection and were filled from the nearest detected frame
finger curls: 17/96 right frames had no hand detection and were filled from the nearest detected frame

root translation: hips_position is a translation offset with an arbitrary origin, so it is de-meaned and added to the canonical hip centre; that keeps the root consistent with the same landmark set the floor height is measured from
canonical landmarks: the right knee sits 19 cm across the body midline from its hip, which a monocular capture of a seated subject does produce. The retarget reproduces it rather than correcting it
canonical landmarks: the right ankle sits 19 cm across the body midline from its hip, which a monocular capture of a seated subject does produce. The retarget reproduces it rather than correcting it

canonical landmarks: the left wrist sits 9 cm across the body midline from its shoulder, which a monocular capture of a seated subject does produce. The retarget reproduces it rather than correcting it

canonical landmarks: the right wrist sits 22 cm across the body midline from its shoulder, which a monocular capture of a seated subject does produce. The retarget reproduces it rather than correcting it
not_represented: the primary object: no glass, cup or other prop is placed. This clip carries 1 `cup` detection(s) over 96 frames, 0 interaction event(s), and no per-frame canonical position for it, so there is no evidence the object was ever grasped or moved. The table's height is still derived from the primary hand's furthest reach -- see set_placement

physics: this is a kinematic replay. The stage carries no rigid bodies, no articulation drives and no contact, so nothing here is a dynamically feasible G1 trajectory -- joint velocity, torque and balance limits are not checked
the head: the G1's 29-DoF configuration has no neck joint, so the subject's head orientation is dropped entirely
ring and little fingers: the Dex3 hand has three fingers, so two of the five CBD finger curls have nowhere to go

thumb abduction: the CBD schema has no thumb abduction channel, so `thumb_0` is driven to 0.6 rad of opposition in proportion to the measured thumb flexion. That is an adapter choice, not a measurement
bones with no rotation signal in the dataset (written as identity, not estimated), so the joints that would have carried them stay at zero: chest, neck, left_shoulder, right_shoulder
face: no face landmarks or blendshapes in the dataset
